subject: [Pulse AI] sudden p99 surge after variant rollout - urgent coordination
body:
-----Original Message-----
From: Evan Cole <evan.cole@pulseai.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: API behavior - sudden latency spikes

Hi Sofia,

We're seeing a sharp spike in p95/p99 latencies for our inference calls to the hosted endpoint starting ~08:50 PST. Error rate is up slightly and throughput looks throttled on our side (many timeouts). This began shortly after our traffic was shifted to the new "pulse-variant" model that was enabled this morning.

Attached is a small sampling of request traces and the dashboard screenshot. This is impacting our synchronous chat flows — several key users are timing out. Can you confirm whether your recent canary/variant rollout touched our cluster and whether there is a rollback plan? We need an ETA on mitigation.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Cole
Head of Platform, Pulse AI
Evan.Cole@pulseai.com

---
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cole <evan.cole@pulseai.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:34:12 -08:00
Subject: Re: API behavior - sudden latency spikes

Evan —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and for the traces. I see the Pulse account had a model variant rollout at 07:45 PST today (pulse-variant v2.3) from our routing logs. We're pulling telemetry now (p99 traces, kernel metrics, batching behavior).

Immediate plan:
- Dylan and I will validate whether the variant changed KV cache behavior and batching parameters.
- If we confirm a regression, we will initiate an automated rollback of the variant to pulse-variant v2.2 for Pulse only (canary rollback, targeted).
- Ben, can you confirm if any infra-level throttles or autoscale events coincided with the rollout?

I will keep you updated every 30 minutes until we stabilize.

Sofia Ivanova
Customer Success — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

---
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:05:37 -08:00
Subject: Re: API behavior - sudden latency spikes

Quick update from telemetry:
- Observed increased tokenization time and a shift in sequence length distribution for Pulse traffic after the variant switch.
- The runtime started using a different attention kernel path for the new quantized variant; p99 CPU on the host jumped ~3.2x for those requests.
- No obvious autoscaler churn; GPU utilization is within expected bounds but host-side queues grew, increasing tail latency.

I'm attaching the raw traces (p99_traces_20261121.zip) and a short notes file (client_request_logs.txt). Initial hypothesis: model variant v2.3 triggers a longer prefix processing path for typical Pulse payloads, exposing a tail path in the serving runtime.

I recommend an immediate targeted traffic shift back to v2.2 for Pulse while we instrument kernel-level telemetry and profile the variant.

-Dylan

---
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:28:43 -08:00
Subject: Re: API behavior - sudden latency spikes

I checked infra events and there was a brief network flap at 08:48 PST on the us-west-2 control plane, but nothing that correlates to host queue growth across all Pulse nodes. No autoscale incidents.

Action I can take now:
- Trigger a targeted rollback of variant for the Pulse account from v2.3 -> v2.2 and pin v2.2 for the next 2 hours (will revert only if rollback fails).
- Open an incident in our internal incident tracker and notify SRE on-call to monitor rollback.

If you approve, I'll execute the rollback and publish a short incident note to the customer.

-Ben

---
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:33:12 -08:00
Subject: Re: API behavior - sudden latency spikes

Please proceed with the targeted rollback now. Marissa, looping you in for exec visibility on Pulse since they are a high-value customer and this will likely trigger a credit request. Lauren, can you prepare a short one-page (bullet) exec note for our leadership and the Pulse execs describing the rollback, root-candidate, and next steps? Include tentative crediting/compensation options.

Evan — we're initiating a targeted rollback for Pulse now; I will confirm when traffic has stabilized. Expect the initial update within 20 minutes.

Sofia

---
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:52:07 -08:00
Subject: Re: API behavior - sudden latency spikes

Rollback executed at 10:50 PST (targeted traffic shift for Pulse to pulse-variant v2.2). On-call SRE is watching.

Preliminary metrics (10:55 PST):
- p95 reduced from 1.42s -> 0.42s for Pulse traffic
- p99 reduced from 3.8s -> 0.78s
- Error rate returned to baseline within 2 minutes

I'll leave the pin for 2 hours unless we see anomalies. Attaching the mitigation_playbook.md I used for the operation.

-Ben

---
From: Evan Cole <evan.cole@pulseai.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Pulse AI Support <support@pulseai.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:02:11 -08:00
Subject: Re: API behavior - sudden latency spikes

Sofia, Ben — thank you. We're seeing latency return to normal and our customers are recovering. We'll keep monitoring but appreciate the quick rollback and pin.

One ask: when you have a moment, can your team share a short postmortem explaining the root cause and timeline? Pulse will need this for our internal incident review. Also please include whether a longer-term mitigation is planned (model tuning, kernel fix, or different quantization).

Best,
Evan

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:22:09 -08:00
Subject: RE: [Pulse AI] sudden p99 surge after variant rollout - urgent coordination

Team —

I've drafted a one-page exec note and an initial timeline. Key points:
- Incident window: 08:50 - 10:50 PST (customer impact peaked ~09:00-10:00).
- Trigger: variant pulse-variant v2.3 rollout exposed a tail kernel used by our runtime for specific tokenization/sequence patterns.
- Immediate mitigation: targeted rollback to v2.2 + 2-hour pin.
- Next steps: profiling run for v2.3 payloads, kernel patch prioritization, and a plan to re-roll with canary smaller audience + additional kernel telemetry.

Attaching the exec note draft and forwarding to Lauren for leadership delivery. I'll prepare a short customer-facing postmortem for Evan by EOD Monday.

-Marissa

---
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 17:02:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: [Pulse AI] sudden p99 surge after variant rollout - urgent coordination

Thanks — I'll finalize and send to leadership + Pulse execs. Draft will cover what happened, actions taken, and two proposed remediation tracks (fast: tune rollout parameters and stricter canary gating; medium: kernel optimization with SRE/Runtime team).

I'll copy the final text to Hari and Leanne for leadership visibility.

-Lauren

[Attachments referenced above: p99_traces_20261121.zip (zip), client_request_logs.txt (text), pulse-dashboard-screenshot.png (image), mitigation_playbook.md (markdown)]
